pr_body:
This implements L2CAP collision mitigation as required by Core Spec Version 5.3 Vol. 3, Part G, Section 5.4, in addition to a test that verifies it. This fixes conformance test L2CAP/TIM/BV-03-C, although changes to auto-pts and the tester application are required.

Fixes #40009

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: EATT bearer L2CAP collision mitigation
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

BT Core Spec:
"If both devices request L2CAP connections (on EATT PSM) simultaneously and both devices
have limited resources, a device may reject the incoming request and find its
own request is also rejected. In this situation, the Central may retry
immediately but the Peripheral shall wait a minimum of 100 ms before retrying;
on LE connections, the Peripheral shall wait at least 2 ×
(connPeripheralLatency + 1) × connInterval if that is longer."

While spec is not requiring any specific behavior when collision occurs (other than not retrying too soon by peripheral), test specification requires that peripheral IUT re-try after mentioned timeout.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
Collision should be detected and either host should retry connection on L2CAP channel or notify application about it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None.

**Additional context**
This is affecting L2CAP/TIM/BV-03-C qualification test case.
comments:
Some comments on this issue:
 -  since this is a GATT requirement on EATT PSM (and not L2CAP protocol one) it should be implemented in GATT/ATT code (ie not directly visible for application, and not implemented in L2CAP code)
 - I think we could have generic timer for establishing EATT as peripheral and then it can also be reused by collision handling
 - in GATT/ATT we can have simple counter on how many retries
 - timer can be possibly randomized (eg min_time + some rand) to improve IOP
@sjanc what's the status here? Still planning an implementation for the 2.7.x series?
Hi,  yes it is on my TODO,  I'll work on that this month
I am currently working on this.

OK, but in `main` I assume? and then you'll backport to v2.7-branch?
I can handle 2.7 backport if needed, once L2CAP/TIM/BV-03-C is passing

> in main I assume? 

Yes, working on top of `main` where we do other EATT work.

> Some comments on this issue:
> 
> * since this is a GATT requirement on EATT PSM (and not L2CAP protocol one) it should be implemented in GATT/ATT code (ie not directly visible for application, and not implemented in L2CAP code)
> * I think we could have generic timer for establishing EATT as peripheral and then it can also be reused by collision handling
> * in GATT/ATT we can have simple counter on how many retries
> * timer can be possibly randomized (eg min_time + some rand) to improve IOP

Im curious about how we come to the conclusion it is a GATT requirement? L2CAP/TIM/BV-03-C seem to be L2CAP specific as well, that said I don't see any new error that can be used for collision detection or the stack is supposed to detect this based on the ongoing connection matching the PSM and checking if all channels are refused with 0x0004 (Connection refused – no resources available) on the response? It would have been a lot clearer if a new error was introduced that way both stacks can confirm a collision has been detected and the retry procedure can start.

Hi,

Yes, those tests are in L2CAP TS but are related to GATT:
"4.15 Generic Attribute Timing tests
Test cases in this group check that the IUT respects the GATT timings."

You may check TSE17840 as well

review_comments: I assume that you've run this and seen the debug message that indicate a collision, right? Because I notice that this test doesn't actually wait for a collision before passing.

A collision will happen because both central and peripheral sends the ecred connection request right after connection. We see this in the log because both fail to allocate ATT channels on receiving the request. Without the fix in this PR, both respond with "No resources" and do not retry the request. Thus zero EATT channels are created and the `num_enhanced != CONFIG_BT_EATT_MAX` check will be true and fail the test.
This may seem a bit cumbersome, but I'd really prefer if the change to this macro (in this file and the samples) were done in a separate commit than the L2CAP commits.
Better to wait for a flag set by a callback.
If this is in L2CAP why this is being implemented for EATT only? It would probably make more sense to implement the retry logic under L2CAP itself and spare ATT of these details.

Hi Luiz,

This is EATT requirement, see https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/40009
Once you've fixed the `default_conn` reference counting there should be an unconditional `bt_conn_unref(default_conn)` before setting it to NULL (and also remove the conditional unref on line 78)
Better to wait for flag set by callback

There is currently no callback to the application when ATT channels are connected. I am planning another PR which makes it possible for the application to connect EATT channels (potentially automatically). A callback can be added then.

I get that there are no callback for ATT, but EATT is dynamic channels, right? Wouldn't the `connected` callback in `bt_l2cap_chan_ops` be called? 

But if we are adding this in a separate PR, please add a TODO here.

`ops->connected` is `bt_att_connected()`, so there is a callback into the ATT layer, but not to the application. I am thinking we can add a callback similar to `att_mtu_updated` that exists in `gatt.c/bt_gatt_cb`.
Typically a GATT user would not need to care about EATT connections. Perhaps we need an ATT callback instead?

Yes, that makes more sense.

When making the api for connecting EATT channels available to the application it needs a way to know that channels are connected. I think the callback should be added in that PR instead and leave the sleep here for now. Will add a TODO.
An API question for that PR: Would it be preferable to have one callback per channel created or per request?
Hmm, given that the stack now will retry requests (possibly with less channels), I think a callback per channel is better, don't you think?

I am not sure.

I have been thinking that we can let `bt_eatt_connect()` take any number of channels to connect and then potentially send multiple requests. In that case per-channel callbacks make more sense. The application does not really care about the on-air requests.

> The application does not really care about the on-air requests.

Agree.

This is where default_conn is set when the connection is initiated, but I just realized this app also supports peripheral mode. In that case you need to check in the connected callback if default_conn is set and if not set it with the help of ref()
If memory serves me correct, only the central needs to unref.
Isn't there a missing return statement here?
When a `FAIL()` statement is reached, the test is aborted.

But the callback function is not returned from (at least looking at the FAIL macro definition). So it still seems to me like the correct thing to do to add the return statement there. Otherwise the code needlessly calls functions like `bt_conn_ref()` and sets `is_connected` to `true`.

IIRC, the `FAIL` macro here will set `bst_result = Failed`, and on the next tick of the simulator it will end the case. 

The `return` is to my understanding not needed (although perhaps nice to have for semantic reasons. @aescolar What is your take?

At the very least there should be a code comment (but I'd still prefer a return statement, even though it doesn't make any practical difference), since for someone not familiar with the simulator it looks very much like a bug.
We have in the LE Audio tests also usually added the return (there are a few cases where we have left it out I see though).
Will add the return.

> The return is to my understanding not needed (although perhaps nice to have for semantic reasons. @aescolar What is your take?

Just for the sake of information: As the fail macro calls `bs_trace_error_time_line()` it will actually exit the simulation there.
Adding the return after certainly does no harm.
The tick checking for != Passed is a minor safety to ensure there is a deadline that causes the test to fail if still "in progress".
